head_commit.message:
Add a HOLD PQB candidate worker with exhaustive ranked sweeps (#18)

* Add a HOLD PQB candidate worker with exhaustive ranked sweeps

PQB (fireblocks-labs/pqb) is a different lock from QSB with different
puzzles, so this is a separate worker and contract, not a change to the
ranked-v2 worker or to any published image.

- vendor/pqb: PQB's CUDA grinder at eccdd09, byte for byte, with its
  licence, notices and provenance hashes.
- research/pqb-ranked: an adaptation of grind.cu that walks a stated
  range exhaustively instead of drawing at random, fails closed when a
  range is not fully accounted for, and reports only gate hits with the
  shape of a DER signature. The SHA-256 and curve arithmetic are
  upstream's.
- contracts/pqb-ranked-v1.json and worker/pqb: range contract, handler,
  file binding, Dockerfile and offline image check.
- docs/pqb/ASSESSMENT.md: evidence, deviations, limits and next gaps.

Evidence is CPU emulation only: complete hit sets equal an independent
enumeration, and pqb's own checker reproduced every hit in a local run.
There is no native GPU run, no timing and no amd64 image build yet. The
modelled saving (12.1 to 8.3 RTX 4090-hours) assumes the ranked sweep
runs at upstream's trial rate, which is unmeasured.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Handle exceptional curve cases exactly in the PQB grinder; add an AWS cost estimate

The device formulas cannot add equal or opposite points or represent
infinity. Every such case puts a zero factor into one of a thread's two
batched inversions, so ec_comb now tests both products, reports a thread
that has one and emits nothing for it, and the host recomputes its
z-blocks with complete affine formulas. Previously such a thread's
points were silently spoiled.

Tested under CPU emulation: with every thread forced through the host
path the hit sets equal the reference on all three stages, and a menu
point planted equal to a z-block's sighash point is reported and handled
exactly. No native GPU evidence; the speed effect is unmeasured.

The assessment gains a desk estimate of AWS cost per spend. It is not a
measurement: only the L40S speed is measured (by pqb), the A10G and L4
speeds are assumed, and prices are aggregator snapshots.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Prepare a native measurement run for the ranked PQB grinder

Preparation only: nothing is launched and nothing here authorizes a
launch.

- research/pqb-ranked/measure: 11 correctness cases with hit sets from
  the independent reference (multi-batch ranges, the DER-shape filter, a
  planted exceptional point) and a one-shot runner that checks them and
  then times upstream's random search against the ranked walk,
  interleaved per stage. Timing is skipped if correctness fails.
- worker/pqb/Dockerfile gains a `measure` stage that compiles upstream's
  unmodified grinder with the same compiler and flags; CI uploads both
  binaries and checks the ranked one is the worker image's.
- scripts/prepare_pqb_measure_bundle.py and
  ops/aws-gpu-execution/host-pqb-measure.sh: the hash-verified bundle
  and the isolated host invocation.
- tests/test_pqb_measure.py dry-runs all of it on emulated binaries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Do not require steady-state rates in the emulated measurement dry run

A slow emulation host may complete too few batches per process in the
short dry run for a steady-state rate. Check whole-process rates there
instead; the runner is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Allow London in the GPU controller's operator config; record refused launches

Every eu-west-1 zone refused a g5.xlarge for capacity on 11 November.
The operator config now accepts eu-west-2 as well as eu-west-1, as the
research controller branch already did; nothing else in the controller
is region-specific. The measurement notes record the three refused
launches: no instance, no measurement, no GPU time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Record the London capacity refusals in the PQB measurement notes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Record the native A10G measurement of the ranked PQB grinder

One g5.xlarge in eu-west-1b on 11 November 2026, public synthetic
fixtures, CI-built binaries of 266f4a0.

- Correctness: all 11 cases returned exactly the reference's hit sets on
  the GPU, including multi-batch ranges, the DER-shape filter and a
  planted exceptional point.
- Timing: the ranked walk ran at 1.004 to 1.014 times upstream's random
  search in steady state, three alternating samples per stage.
- A10G rates 2.49 / 2.73 / 2.01 G trials/s, about 0.42 of pqb's
  published RTX 4090 rates. The cost table now uses the measured speed:
  about $22 per spend on-demand in eu-west-1 with exhaustive sweeps.
- Round-0 units take up to 21 minutes on this card, longer than the
  application's 900-second job timeout; the provisional unit size must
  shrink before a contract freeze.

Seven launches were refused for capacity before this one; none
allocated an instance. Estimated compute about $0.13. Cleanup verified,
with one irregularity described in the record. Component measurement:
no full solve, no whole-spend time, not a bill.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Resize PQB work units to fit a 900-second job limit (pqb-ranked-v2)

At the A10G rates measured on 11 November, pqb-ranked-v1's round-0
units took up to 21 minutes, longer than the application's job timeout.

pqb-ranked-v2: pinning units of 14 nSequence values (divides the usable
values exactly), round-0 units of 3 * 2^27 prefixes, round-1 units of
2^30 prefixes. The largest unit of each stage is 486 s, 502 s and 486 s
at the measured rates. This is a sizing choice from one host's rates;
no full unit has been run.

The partition changed, so the search version changed. v1 was
provisional and never published or enrolled; its contract file is
replaced.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix the PQB review findings

- grind.cu: range bounds are checked before any sum, so a huge count
  cannot wrap past the check; range options must be unsigned decimals
  and need the option that turns ranked mode on; QG_FUSE=0 is refused
  at compile time, since the unfused kernel would hash the stale point
  slots of a thread the exceptional path skipped. No kernel or
  range-walk code changed.
- run_measure.py: any error in the timing phase is recorded and the
  result is always written; the last stratum can no longer run past the
  prefix space.
- Dockerfile: the measure stage is no longer last, so a build without
  --target gives the worker.
- CI: the artifact records the branch head, not the merge commit of a
  pull_request run.
- Worker timeout 840 s, under a 900-second job limit.
- The emulation build cache refuses a temp directory it does not own.
- Docs: the unranked path is not upstream's binary; the native A10G
  result applies to the new binary by review, not by measurement.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: artifact binding, assessment cost summary, timeout race

- CI records the commit that was actually checked out and built
  (GITHUB_SHA) and the event name. On a pull_request run that is the
  merge commit, so the bundle script refuses that artifact and says to
  use the push run's. The previous change labelled merge-tree binaries
  with the head SHA.
- The assessment's cost-and-cleanup summary reports the paid A10G
  session, its estimated cost (not provider billing) and the irregular
  but verified cleanup, instead of saying no hardware was used.
- The handler tolerates a grinder that exits between the timeout and
  the signal, and still returns an uncredited 'interrupted' result.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Prepare bound PQB full-unit validation and correct evidence status

* Require push artifacts for full-unit native validation

* Address review: enforce the kernel's slot spacing; bound the cross-check's locktime

- The round kernel handles at most three deletion boundaries per
  64-byte block, which needs boundaries 22 bytes apart. The handler and
  the grinder's host check allowed 12 (upstream's check, weaker than
  its kernel), so a crafted table could be hashed wrongly and still be
  reported complete. Both now require 22; PQB's own table has exactly 22.
- pqb_crosscheck.py also checks a pinning hit's nSequence and nLockTime
  against the requested range, not only the whole-sequence nonce span.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: filtered cases that must emit; keep failed invocations

- expected.json gains two DER-filtered pinning cases whose expected set
  holds a shaped candidate (compressed and uncompressed encodings),
  computed by the reference. The only filtered case so far expected no
  candidate, so a build that counted gate hits but dropped every
  filtered candidate would have passed. The 11 November native run did
  not include these; the docs now say so.
- run_measure keeps a failed invocation's problem, arguments and whole
  stdout, stderr and hits under failed-invocations/ beside the result;
  the full-unit runner does the same for its preflight, and the
  measurement host script collects nested files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: keep wrong-answer artifacts, require steady state, reject duplicate events

- run_measure keeps an invocation's problem, arguments, stdout, stderr
  and hits when it exits 0 with a result that is not the expected one,
  not only on a timeout or non-zero exit.
- A run no longer passes unless every upstream and ranked sample reached
  steady state. The emulated dry run, which cannot, turns the
  requirement off explicitly and the result records it.
- A second @setup, @range or @done line fails the invocation instead of
  replacing the first; a malformed event line fails it too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: do not credit a unit whose candidates repeat

The handler checked candidate count, capacity and syntax but not
uniqueness, so a grinder that wrote one hit twice with a matching count
was credited as range-complete, while the full-unit acceptance path
rejects duplicates. Each trial is visited once; a repeated line now
fails the unit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Record native PQB full-unit receipts and evidence limits

* Clarify executed and skipped local test counts

* Retain PQB setup failures and add correctness-only native validation

* Add pinned consumer CPU compatibility validation

* Record native filter validation, consumer compatibility and PQB image scan

* Prepare bounded public PQB solve through the real Batch consumer transport

* Bind mineable consumer policy and retain the known preflight without resubmission

* Restore pinned upstream policy and recheck known pinning jobs on handover

* Prepare independent upstream checks for real public solve hits

* Audit emitted public hits and negative CPU decisions against upstream

* Bind upstream checks to the pinned native curve backend

* Delete disabled Batch queues without an ignored empty association update

* Record the complete public PQB transport solve and verified cleanup

* Address review: checksum artifact identity, paginate cleanup check, durable handoff, publisher failure receipt

- CI adds source-commit and source-event to the artifact's SHA256SUMS,
  and the bundle script requires the list to name exactly the five
  files and checks each. A swapped or mixed-in identity file no longer
  passes.
- The public-solve controller follows NextMarker when checking for its
  cleanup function, instead of trusting the first 50 results.
- The MCP handoff flushes the request file and its directory entry
  before the request can be dispatched.
- The private publisher records a terminal failed receipt, with the
  stage reached and whether the registry state is uncertain, when
  anything fails after its one-shot marker.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: atomic receipt, retried cancellation, whole-log scan, earlier trap, full report checks

- The private publisher writes its success receipt to a temporary file,
  flushes it and replaces the marker, so a crash cannot leave a
  truncated receipt for a published image.
- The public-solve controller keeps cancellation intent and confirmation
  apart: a cancel the provider rejected is retried on the next pass and
  in the failure path instead of being skipped.
- The worker handler scans the whole log for completion lines, so a
  second one more than a megabyte back is still counted.
- The full-unit host script arms its collection trap with the one-shot
  marker, before the metadata writes.
- A correctness case also requires the completion report to count the
  hits written and to name the range and filter it was given, as the
  worker's range_report does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: push artifacts only, checked timing samples, atomic result, removal after a failed arm

- The measurement bundle requires a push-run artifact, as the full-unit
  bundler does: a pull_request artifact is refused even with its merge
  commit checked out.
- A ranked timing sample must name the range and filter it was asked
  for, report the z-block count this script computes for that range,
  and count the hit lines it wrote. A stale or different workload is no
  longer accepted as the sample.
- The runner replaces its result file whole (temporary file, flush,
  rename, directory flush).
- The public-solve controller's remove step looks the launch template
  up by campaign name, so a campaign whose arm failed before recording
  the template id can still be removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: resumable removal, durable failure receipt, device record, exact Lambda request

- public-solve remove: every deletion tolerates a resource that is
  already gone, so an interrupted removal can be rerun to the end, and
  job definitions are found by name so a registration whose response
  was lost is still deregistered.
- The private publisher's failure receipt is flushed and renamed like
  its success receipt.
- A measurement result passes only if its probe named the device, and
  only a GPU counts; the emulated dry run allows the CPU build
  explicitly and the result records it.
- GPU controller: the cleanup archive is byte-stable and written at
  prepare. In MCP mode arm requires the staged S3 object and persists
  that exact CreateFunction request, settled before the deadline
  starts; the CLI path still sends the ZIP inline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: more removal discovery, durable markers, gate-hit check, bound baseline, staged archive

- public-solve remove finds an unrecorded security group by campaign
  name and VPC.
- Full-unit receipts and the private publisher's one-shot marker are
  flushed to disk (file and directory); the marker is created
  exclusively before anything else.
- The public-solve controller refuses to credit a completed unit whose
  24-bit gate-hit count does not fit the unit's size (trials computed
  from the checked range; 6 sigma + 6, as in the full-unit harness).
  The self-test's fixtures report a consistent count. Not run: the
  self-test needs the pinned consumer checkout.
- build.py checks the upstream grinder against the lock before the
  measure stage compiles it as the timing baseline.
- The public-solve cleanup archive is byte-stable, written with its
  hash at prepare, and rebuilt and checked before arm changes phase.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
